_description: Canonical enumeration of `#log/*` and `#status/*` system-utility tag subtype values. Source of truth for the pre-write-guard hook's near-match DENY discipline (R-05) and the librarian log-subtype-canonical audit. Foundation seeds the operational subtypes that ship with foundation skills + crons; adopters extend via Layer 3 overlay at `log_subtype_registry_overlay.json` (sibling location post-install).

_design_notes.consumer: pre-write-guard.sh tag-validation branch (R-05 near-match DENY); librarian log-subtype-canonical capability (audit-time drift detection); skill-side `log_subtype:` SKILL.md declaration contract
_design_notes.lockstep_pair: governance/tagging-rules.json R-05 (tag-validation branch) + System Governance - Tagging.md (narrative spoke) + hooks/pre-write-guard.sh (enforcement) + governance/tagging-rules.json#taxonomy.system_utility_governance
_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 documentary lockstep — registry additions move with tagging-rules.json R-05 + System Governance - Tagging.md narrative spoke + pre-write-guard.sh tag-validation branch + tagging-rules.json#taxonomy.system_utility_governance in one commit. NO write-time DENY for R-37, by design (git commit-boundary atomicity + librarian governance-parity-audit). Adopter-side additions land at the sibling overlay (log_subtype_registry_overlay.json); no foundation-repo commit required for adopter operational subtypes.

log_subtypes.description: End-of-session reconciliation artifacts emitted by the session-close skill or its manual invocation. One file per session.

Error artifacts emitted by ANY cron wrapper on non-zero exit. owner_cron is null because the subtype is shared across all cron wrappers (each cron emits cron-error on its own failure); no single cron owns the registry entry. One file per failure; preserves stderr + invocation context.
Output emitted by the log-archive librarian capability. Documents which files were rotated to Archive/Logs/.
Build-progress logs emitted during plan execution (foundation-repo install, scaffold rendering, capability deploy).
Documentation-emission logs (capability docs rendered, narrative spokes generated, ADRs authored).
Backlog-hygiene capability output. Surfaces stale items, lifecycle timeouts, auto-archive candidates.
Digest pipeline run output (calendar + chat + meeting synthesis). Daily cadence typical.
Inventory-walk outputs (vault filesystem inventory, manifest regeneration runs, packet-coverage scans).

status_subtypes.description: Marks a file as processed by the appropriate pipeline (meeting-processor, inbox-archive, etc.). The frontmatter `processed:` boolean is canonical; the tag mirrors it for graph-view filterability.
Flagged for operator review. Used on auto-emitted content that needs a triage gate.

_status_subtypes_design_notes.scope: Processing-state values only — `#status/*` tag dimension governs whether a file has been processed by its appropriate pipeline (meeting-processor, inbox-archive, reconcile-day, etc.). Three canonical values: processed, pending, needs-review.
_status_subtypes_design_notes.out_of_scope: Lifecycle-state values (e.g., `active`, `paused`, `complete`, etc. — exact enum varies per archetype) are NOT in this registry. They live at frontmatter `status:` field per archetype-conditional-fields. The schema enforces the per-archetype enum at write-time; the tag dimension stays focused on processing-state. Tagging files with lifecycle-state values via `#status/*` is NOT the supported pattern.
_status_subtypes_design_notes.rationale: Blending processing-state and lifecycle-state under the same `#status/*` tag dimension seeds adopter confusion. The two semantic classes are kept separate: tagging covers operational processing; frontmatter `status:` covers archetype lifecycle.
